question: Part IV-A of the Constitution of India contains _____________ Articles.
solution:
The correct answer is __**one**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Part IV-A of the Constitution of India contains only one Article, which is Article 51A.
 
• Article 51A specifies the Fundamental Duties of every citizen of India.
 
• The Fundamental Duties were added by the 42nd Amendment Act in 1976.
 
• These duties are inspired by the Constitution of the former Soviet Union and aim to remind citizens of their responsibilities toward the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fundamental Duties**

 
 
• The Fundamental Duties are listed in Article 51A under Part IV-A of the Constitution of India.
 
• There are currently 11 Fundamental Duties, which include obligations such as respecting the Constitution, the National Flag, and the National Anthem, cherishing the noble ideals of the freedom struggle, and protecting the sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India.
 
• These duties also encompass promoting harmony, safeguarding public property, and striving for excellence in all spheres of individual and collective activity.
 
• Fundamental Duties are non-justiciable, meaning they are not legally enforceable by the courts for their violation.
 
 
 
• **42nd Amendment Act, 1976**
 
 
• The 42nd Amendment Act, also known as the "Mini-Constitution," was enacted during the Emergency period by the Indira Gandhi government.
 
• This amendment brought significant changes to the Constitution, including the addition of Fundamental Duties, changes to the Preamble, and various provisions strengthening the central government's power.
 
• It is considered one of the most controversial amendments due to the extent of changes it introduced.
 
 
 
• **Soviet Union's Influence**
 
 
• The concept of Fundamental Duties in the Indian Constitution was inspired by the Constitution of the former Soviet Union.
 
• The Soviet Constitution emphasized the duties of citizens towards the state and society, which influenced the drafting of similar duties in India.
